title: Gerrit mode
subtitle: Push for review, patch sets in the graph

lines.say: Gerrit is a code review server used by projects like Android and Chromium. It doesn't use pushed branches. You push your commit to a special ref, and every amend becomes a new patch set of the same change.

props.title: One commit, many patch sets
props.items:
GitCommit | Commit | With a Change-Id trailer
CloudUpload | Push for review | HEAD to refs/for/main
Pencil | Amend | Same Change-Id, new patch set
Check | Merged | Gerrit submits the change

lines.say: Git Gud notices when a repository talks to Gerrit: a dot gitreview file, a Change-Id hook, or a Gerrit-looking host. It offers Gerrit mode in a banner.
Enable it and confirm the host, the project and the target branch. Nothing changes for repositories that don't use Gerrit.

sections.title: Changes in the graph
sections.intent: Open changes as nodes, patch sets.

lines.say: Now the open changes on the server appear in the graph, each with a dashed pill and its change number.
Select one, and the detail panel lists every patch set: when it was uploaded and what kind of change it was. A button opens the change in your browser.
The toolbar switch shows only the latest patch set of each change, or all of them.
Push for review becomes the main button. Choose the target branch, add a topic if you like, and mark it work in progress or private.
Git Gud pushes HEAD to refs for main. If Gerrit refuses, for example because the Change-Id is missing, you get a message that says how to fix it.
And amending is welcome here. Instead of a force-push warning, Git Gud tells you the amend will become a new patch set.
